newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares recoup losses to end slightly down.
newsitem.headline: German shares recoup losses to end slightly down.

text.p: German shares finished the day on Monday slightly lower, having bounced off earlier lows following a firmer opening on Wall Street and the support of a stronger dollar.
The IBIS DAX index ended the day down 4.37 points, or 0.16 percent, at 2,655.49 points.
The 30-share blue chip DAX index earlier ended down 7.19 points, or 0.27 percent, at 2,651.85 points.
Support over the course of trade came from the dollar, which was steady at a strong 1.52 against the mark and a firm opening on Wall Street in afternoon electronic trade boosted the market

Profit-taking hit the chemical sector particularly hard. BASF AG extended its losses from Friday, when it fell on news that a U.S. advisory committee had recommending withholding approval for a new BASF drug, Meridia.
BASF recovered somewhat over the session to end bourse down 10 pfennigs at 48 marks. BASF shares ended the IBIS session up a pfennig at 48.15 marks.
Degussa AG ended bourse trade down 2.50 marks at 552.50 marks, again hit by profit-taking after having earlier risen on news it planned to up its stake in U.S.-based Muro Pharmaceuticals.
Degussa closed IBIS trading down 2.40 marks at 555.00 marks
